Quando você pede ou diz o que come, o al: When you order or say what you eat, the food goes into the accusative (the direct object). Only feminine words in -а change: -а becomes -у. Masculine and neuter nouns that are not living beings stay the same: «Я хочу рис», «Я хочу мясо», «Я хочу салат». English never marks this, so it is easy to forget: the word after the verb must change when it is feminine.

Em russo, muitas ideias de necessidade e: In Russian, many ideas of need and permission do not have a subject like "I". The person who needs goes into the dative (мне, тебе, ему...) and the word «нужно» comes after. After it can come an infinitive verb: «Мне нужно работать». If a noun follows, the form of «нужно» agrees with it: «нужен» (masculine), «нужна» (feminine), «нужно» (neuter), «нужны» (plural). But «можно» (it is allowed) and «нельзя» (it is not allowed) never change: they are adverbs.
em português dizemos «eu preciso de água: in English we say "I need water", with "I" as the subject. In Russian it is "to me is needed water" (Мне нужна вода), and «нужна» agrees with the water.
